The source says "plausible report", meaning one that only looks credible. The target says "विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट तैयार कर सकता है", which asserts trustworthiness and blunts the warning. "भरोसेमंद दिखने वाली" fixes it. The issue is minor and does not block.

The target header "कौन-सा रूट गलत होगा" follows the source "What would be a bad route" closely. The awkward header-to-cell relationship, where the cells list tasks, comes from the source. The table is understandable in context. This is not a translation defect and is not worth a change request.

The target says "पिछले बेक-ऑफ में वह जीत गया था". "बेक-ऑफ" in Devanagari is a transliterated Western idiom that many Hindi-speaking developers will not know. The rest of the text keeps English technical terms in Latin script. Adding a gloss such as "मुकाबले (bake-off)" is a small improvement. This is minor.

The source has the dry beat "That scorer is not glamorous. That is the point." The target "यही बात महत्वपूर्ण है" turns it into a flat, formal statement, and "चमकदार चीज़" is stiffer than the source. A more idiomatic punchline such as "यही तो असली बात है" would keep the voice. This is polish.

The target uses Devanagari for core terms early: "राउटर", "रूट", "स्कोरर", "एजेंट". Later it switches to Latin script: "Router के विरुद्ध experiments", "Route accuracy", "Mastra agent", "scorer". The same concepts appear in both scripts, which is noticeable across the article and looks inconsistent. It is not a fact or code error, so it is not blocking. The article needs a single convention.

The source says the router "cannot consistently produce valid JSON and pick the obvious specialist". Logically, that means distrust follows if either check fails. The target, "valid JSON consistently produce नहीं कर सकता और स्पष्ट specialist चुनने में विफल रहता है", makes distrust depend on both failures happening together. That is a real logical shift, so it needs fixing. I rate it 3, not 4: the code right above it throws separately for `valid-router-json < 1` and `route-accuracy < 0.9`, so the technical behaviour stays clear. Use "या" and fold "लगातार" into the sentence, as suggested.

"Mastra में ज़रूरी सतहें मौजूद हैं" carries over the physical meaning of the software jargon "surfaces" ("Mastra has the surfaces"). It reads as translationese right in the introduction, where a credible local voice matters most. The list that follows makes the meaning recoverable, so this is not a blocker. Still, "साधन" or "सुविधाएँ" states the practical meaning without adding any new claim.

This duplicates 910dd7c3 on the same fragment, "ज़रूरी सतहें मौजूद हैं". I agree for the same reason: the literal "surfaces" is noticeable translationese in the introduction. "सुविधाएँ" works, and the following list keeps the specifics. Fix both issues with a single edit.

The source, "Evals reward boring seams", is just as terse. English readers also have to infer what "seams" means from the next paragraph, and the target keeps that paragraph: "downstream specialist के चलने से पहले ही route को टेस्ट किया जा सकता है". Leaving "seams" as a Latin technical term fits the article's own mixed-script convention. The suggested rewrite ("साफ़, अलग से टेस्ट की जा सकने वाली boundaries काम आती हैं") would flatten the dry, clipped line the policy wants preserved. This is an optional preference, not a defect.

This duplicates c37932a4, and I reject it for the same reason. "Evals को उबाऊ seams पसंद आते हैं" mirrors the terse source line "Evals reward boring seams", and the target's next paragraph already explains that the route is tested on its own. The suggested "सीधी-सादी सीमाएँ ही काम आती हैं" swaps the jargon for a vaguer word and loses the clipped voice. It is a stylistic preference, not an error.

The source, "production scar tissue", means painful, hard-won lessons, and that pain is why the "Other" row matters. The target's "production का जमा हुआ अनुभव" neutralizes it into generic "experience". The policy asks for idioms to be recreated, not sanitized. A phrase like "production में खाई ठोकरों/चोटों के निशान" would restore the edge without adding any facts.

This duplicates 0f8430e2 on the same fragment, "\"अन्य\" में production का जमा हुआ अनुभव रहता है". The originator rated it 2. I rate it 3 because the policy explicitly warns against a sanitized vendor-blog voice, and this line strips the attitude from "scar tissue". Fix both issues with a single edit that uses a wound or scar image.

"लक्ष्य है system को reason करना आसान बनाना" puts "system" as the object of the verb "reason". That reads as "making it easy to reason the system", which is not idiomatic even in Hinglish. The source's "easier to reason about" is about understanding the system's behaviour, and this sentence is the section's thesis. Something like "system कैसे बर्ताव करता है, यह समझना आसान बनाना" fixes it.

This duplicates d808b889, and I agree. The fragment "system को reason करना" misrepresents the "reason about" relationship in the section's key sentence. Either suggested fix works if it stays short; fix both issues with a single edit.

The source's "saves you four figures a month" is kept in magnitude, so no quantity is lost. But "आपके चार अंकों वाले खर्च को बचा ले" reads as saving a four-figure expense, not as saving a four-figure amount. "हर महीने चार अंकों की रकम बचा दे" is more natural and just as accurate. This is minor polish.

The source's "makes everyone feel temporarily adult" mocks a feeling of professional responsibility. The target's "सबको खुद को वयस्क महसूस कराए" uses the literal age sense of "adult", and the joke falls flat. The suggested "लगे कि अब हम ज़िम्मेदार लोग हैं" rebuilds the sarcasm. The meaning survives, so this is polish (2), not a blocker.
This duplicates 791b39df on the same fragment, "खुद को वयस्क महसूस कराए". I agree: the literal "वयस्क" weakens the dry punchline. Fix both issues with a single edit.

In "Evals से evils से लड़ें!", the two uses of "से" do different grammatical jobs ("with" and "against") next to each other, so the title stumbles. The Evals/evils sound pun does survive, because both English words are kept. That makes this polish, not severity 3. "Evals के सहारे evils से लड़ें!" fixes it; keep the `/llm-evals-are-broken` URL unchanged.

This duplicates e3fb120a on "[Evals से evils से लड़ें!](/llm-evals-are-broken)". I agree the double "से" is clumsy. I disagree that the pun is lost, since both words remain. It is minor, and one edit fixes both issues.

"बचना" is intransitive, so the ergative subject "इसने" in "क्या इसने ... इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?" is ungrammatical. It should be "क्या यह ... से बचा?". The meaning is still clear, so this is minor polish.

The source's "plausible report" means a report that only looks believable. The target's "एक विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट" means a trustworthy report, which contradicts the warning: a report missing its evidence is exactly what should not be trusted. I raise this to 3 because it slightly changes the meaning in an argument about hidden failures. "भरोसेमंद दिखने वाली रिपोर्ट" fixes it.

The header "कौन-सा रूट गलत होगा" asks which route would be wrong. The cells, such as "लंबे संदर्भ का सारांश, सरल वर्गीकरण", list tasks that should not go to that route. The source's "What would be a bad route" means sending those tasks there. "यहाँ भेजना गलत रूटिंग होगी" matches the column. This is minor, because readers can work it out.

The source's "won the last bake-off" is an American idiom. The target just transliterates it as "पिछले बेक-ऑफ में", which many Hindi-speaking developers will not recognize. The policy asks for idioms to be recreated. "मुकाबला" or "benchmark की होड़" keeps the meaning. This is minor polish, because the sentence still makes sense.

The source's "That is the point." is a dry punchline. The target's "यही बात महत्वपूर्ण है" turns it into a flat, formal statement. "और यही तो असली बात है" keeps the voice. The meaning is intact, so this is polish.

The target writes the same core terms in Devanagari early on ("राउटर के लिए मैं चार अक्षों", "रूट सटीकता") and in Latin script later ("router prompt बदला", "Route accuracy"), even for the same concepts. Mixing scripts is normal in Indian tech Hindi, but switching one recurring term back and forth is noticeable. This is a consistency polish issue, and it does not affect meaning.

Source requires both abilities: “produce valid JSON and pick the obvious specialist.” Target separately negates them and joins failures with “नहीं कर सकता और … विफल रहता है”, making both failures necessary for distrust. Use “लगातार valid JSON नहीं दे सकता या सही specialist नहीं चुन सकता” so either failure disqualifies production trust.

“ज़रूरी सतहें” renders “surfaces” physically, obscuring the facilities immediately listed as scorers, datasets and experiments. “ज़रूरी साधन” preserves their practical role. It loses the interface metaphor but gains immediate Hindi clarity without changing the claim.

“उबाऊ seams पसंद आते हैं” leaves the architectural point obscure. Source clarifies it with “test the route before the downstream specialist runs.” Prefer “Evals के लिए हिस्सों को अलग से टेस्ट करने की सीधी-सादी boundaries काम आती हैं।” This sacrifices the compact personification while retaining the endorsement of unglamorous test boundaries.

“जमा हुआ अनुभव” preserves experience but loses the painful learning in “production scar tissue.” “Production में खाई ठोकरों के निशान” recreates that edge through a natural Hindi metaphor. The point remains understandable, so severity 3 overstates this localized tonal loss.

“system को reason करना” is an awkward verb construction at the section’s central conclusion. Source says “easier to reason about.” “लक्ष्य है कि सिस्टम का व्यवहार समझना और उसके बारे में तर्क करना आसान हो” restores the relationship explicitly; it gains clarity without losing the reasoning component.

“चार अंकों वाले खर्च को बचा ले” awkwardly attaches the magnitude to expenditure, whereas “saves you four figures a month” states savings. “हर महीने चार अंकों की रकम बचा दे” is clearer and preserves the unspecified currency. As the claim acknowledges, no changed quantity is demonstrated; this merits severity 2.

“सबको खुद को वयस्क महसूस कराए” is cumbersome and makes “feel temporarily adult” sound literal. “जिसे देखकर सबको थोड़ी देर के लिए लगे कि अब हम ज़िम्मेदार लोग हैं” recreates the professional-maturity joke. It loses the age image but gains a natural sarcastic closing beat.

“Evals से evils से लड़ें!” stacks two differently functioning instances of “से”, making the title stumble. “Evils से लड़ें, Evals के साथ!” preserves the words and sound-play of “Fight Evils with Evals!” while clarifying their roles. Keep the existing URL.

In “क्या इसने … इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?”, the intransitive “बचा” does not take the ergative subject “इसने”. Change it to “क्या यह … इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?” The meaning of “Did it avoid” is already recoverable; this is minor grammar repair.

Source “a plausible report” concerns apparent credibility despite missing evidence. Target “एक विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट” can assert actual trustworthiness. “भरोसेमंद दिखने वाली रिपोर्ट” makes the warning precise. Context already signals the problem, so the modest severity is appropriate.

“कौन-सा रूट गलत होगा” asks for a route name, but cells contain tasks such as “सरल वर्गीकरण”. Source “What would be a bad route” is also compressed, but the Hindi can state the intended relationship clearly: “यहाँ क्या नहीं भेजना चाहिए”. This preserves the table’s task-to-route distinction.

“production का जमा हुआ अनुभव” softens “production scar tissue” into neutral experience. “Production में खाई ठोकरों के निशान” restores hard-earned pain using a familiar Hindi image. This is the same limited tonal defect as issue 0f8430e28f4d9abefcc1, not an additional meaning failure.

“पिछले बेक-ऑफ में वह जीत गया था” retains the competitive comparison in “won the last bake-off”; “जीत गया” supplies contextual meaning. The packet does not establish that most intended developers find the term unfamiliar. “पिछले मॉडल मुकाबले” is an available adaptation, but the preference does not establish a defect.

The problem is stronger than the word “वयस्क” alone: “सबको खुद को वयस्क महसूस कराए” makes the closing joke syntactically wooden. Source “feel temporarily adult” mocks temporary maturity. “सबको थोड़ी देर के लिए लगे कि अब हम ज़िम्मेदार लोग हैं” retains that purpose, exchanging literal adulthood for natural sarcasm.

“Evals से evils से लड़ें!” has an awkward double “से”, so repair is warranted. However, the claim that the pun is lost is too strong: both “Evals” and “evils” remain. “Evils से लड़ें, Evals के साथ!” clarifies the grammar while retaining the source wordplay and URL.

“यह स्कोरर कोई चमकदार चीज़ नहीं है। यही बात महत्वपूर्ण है।” preserves the two-beat reversal of “not glamorous. That is the point.” The second sentence is slightly more formal, but the dry endorsement remains intelligible. “यही तो बात है” is optional tightening, not a demonstrated voice failure.

Target alternates recognizable equivalents such as “रूट” and “route”, while retaining identifiers such as `code`. The quoted “Mastra agent … route चुनने” is natural technical Hindi and creates no competing meaning. A uniform script convention could improve house-style consistency, but none is required by the supplied policy.

“ज़रूरी सतहें मौजूद हैं” does not naturally convey the evaluation facilities meant by “has the surfaces”. The following scorers/datasets/experiments list supports “ज़रूरी साधन मौजूद हैं”. This replaces the spatial image with its practical meaning, gaining clarity while preserving the introduction’s purpose.

Source “make the system easier to reason about” is not naturally conveyed by “system को reason करना”. The proposed “सिस्टम का व्यवहार समझना और उसके बारे में तर्क करना आसान हो” preserves both comprehension and reasoning. The current text has not repaired this central concluding statement.

“Evals को उबाऊ seams पसंद आते हैं” preserves words from “Evals reward boring seams” without clearly conveying separately testable boundaries. Source “test the route before the downstream specialist runs” supports making that connection explicit. Use “अलग से टेस्ट करने की सीधी-सादी boundaries”; avoid the suggested “ही”, which adds exclusivity absent from the source.

Target: 'क्या इसने नीरस काम के लिए प्रीमियम मॉडल इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?'. 'बचना' is intransitive here, so the ergative 'इसने' is ungrammatical. It should be 'क्या यह ... से बचा?'. The source question, 'Did it avoid premium models for boring work?', is plain. This sits in the prominent four-axes table and is a visible error, but it does not change the meaning.

Source: '"Other" is where the production scar tissue lives.' Target: 'production का जमा हुआ अनुभव रहता है।' The target says neutral 'accumulated experience'. The source's point is that hard-won incident pain is what makes the catch-all row matter, and the target drops that edge. This is an idiom that policy says to recreate, and the target only flattens it. An image like 'ठोकरों से मिली सीख' would fix it.

Target: 'जो कुछ समय के लिए सबको खुद को वयस्क महसूस कराए।' The double object 'सबको खुद को' is clumsy. The literal 'वयस्क' blurs the dry jab in the source ('makes everyone feel temporarily adult'), which is about performative maturity. The meaning is recoverable, so this is polish rather than a blocker. A smoother form would be 'सबको थोड़ी देर के लिए समझदार-वयस्क होने का एहसास करा दे'.

Target: 'Evals से evils से लड़ें!' Source: 'Fight Evils with Evals!' The two 'से' mean 'with' and 'from', so the pun reads clunky and ambiguous, and it appears in the body text and the Resources list. 'Evals के दम पर evils से लड़ें!' keeps the wordplay and clarifies the syntax. This is a link label, so the URL stays unchanged. It is minor and not blocking.

Target: 'JSON validity, allowed tools और traceability की अपनी checks होनी चाहिए।' 'Check' is commonly used as feminine in Hindi dev speech, so 'अपनी checks' agrees. It also conveys the source's 'get their own checks' directly. The proposed 'हर एक की अलग जाँच' is a valid alternative, not a defect.

Source: 'produce a plausible report without preserving evidence'. Target: 'एक विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट तैयार कर सकता है'. 'Plausible' means convincing-looking but possibly wrong. 'विश्वसनीय' means trustworthy, which reads as the report actually being reliable and weakens the sentence's warning. 'सुनने में ठोस लगने वाली' or 'प्रशंसनीय-सी दिखने वाली' fixes it.

Target: 'Mastra में ज़रूरी सतहें मौजूद हैं'. Source: 'has the surfaces'. 'सतहें' is a word-for-word calque of the API-surface sense, so a Hindi developer would not parse it naturally. The same word recurs in the 'एक सतह' usage elsewhere. 'APIs/टूल' would read as credible local writing.

This duplicates 6c5e5a5c61a58a4eefdc. Target: '"अन्य" में production का जमा हुआ अनुभव रहता है।' The source's 'scar tissue' carries accumulated incident pain, and the neutral wording loses that. The defect is real and still present in the current text.

Terminology drifts within the article. The opening and tables use Devanagari: 'राउटर', 'रूट', 'बग ट्रैजेक्टरी में छिपे होते हैं'. Later the text switches to Latin: 'Router के विरुद्ध experiments', 'Route accuracy', and 'Trajectory' in the layers table. One term appears in two scripts, which is noticeably inconsistent. Mixed script is normal for Indian developers, but a stable per-term convention is expected.

Target: 'आपका मॉडल राउटर डिस्पैच टेबल के साथ बस अंदाज़ों का खेल है।' Source: 'vibes with a dispatch table'. This recreates the idiom in natural Hindi and keeps the dry dismissal and the 'dispatch table' image. 'Vibes' is slang, and 'अंदाज़ों का खेल' carries the same attitude. Keeping the English word 'vibes' would be an optional alternative. The rationale for the adaptation belongs in the negotiation, not in the article text.
This duplicates c6ebe3efcaefed77af8e. Target: 'सबको खुद को ... महसूस कराए' is the same clumsy double-object construction. It is minor polish, not a meaning error.

This duplicates 491603b9ca1c18f8f085. Target: 'क्या इसने नीरस काम के लिए प्रीमियम मॉडल इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?' The ergative 'इसने' with intransitive 'बचा' is ungrammatical. A correct form is 'क्या यह ... से बचा?' or 'क्या इसने ... से परहेज़ किया?'.

Target: 'valid JSON consistently produce नहीं कर सकता और स्पष्ट specialist चुनने में विफल रहता है'. Source: 'cannot consistently produce valid JSON and pick the obvious specialist'. The English adverb is left inside the first clause, which is awkward code-switching, and it no longer covers the second clause. Hindi 'लगातार' would govern both. The English verbs are also stranded ('produce नहीं कर सकता').

Source: 'Evals reward boring seams.' Target: 'Evals को उबाऊ seams पसंद आते हैं।' 'Seams' is kept as an opaque English word with no gloss, and the preceding sentence ('यह थोड़ा कृत्रिम है। अच्छा है।') is what gives it meaning. 'पुरस्कृत' also became 'पसंद आते हैं'. A reader who does not know the testing-seam idea cannot reconstruct the metaphor. A short gloss such as 'साफ़ जोड़ (seams)' would fix it.

Target: 'अब बातचीत का स्वर बदल जाता है।' Source: 'Now the conversation changes.' The following example moves from 'बेहतर लगता है' to numeric comparisons and then 'engineering conversation', which fits a change in the tenor of the discussion. The nuance is faithful to the passage and adds no new factual claim. 'बातचीत ही बदल जाती है' is an equally valid alternative.

The issue itself is rated severity 1 (valid alternative). It duplicates a6cd596e7e6fcced6f8e, which covers the same 'Evals से evils से लड़ें!' label at severity 2. It is nonblocking, and the fix is tracked in the other issue.

Target: 'valid JSON consistently produce नहीं कर सकता और स्पष्ट specialist चुनने में विफल रहता है'. Two negative predicates joined by 'और' read as a condition where both must fail before trust is withdrawn. The surrounding scorer logic (valid-router-json and route-accuracy as separate gates) means either failure is disqualifying. The English ('cannot ... produce valid JSON and pick') is similarly ambiguous but less so, and Hindi 'या' would remove the ambiguity. It misleads mildly rather than reversing the argument, so I hold it at 3, not 4.

The two named specific flaws are real: 'scar tissue' becomes neutral 'जमा हुआ अनुभव', and 'boring seams' is left as unglossed English. Other metaphors are handled well, such as 'अंदाज़ों का खेल' and 'retire' for averages. The aggregate stays open until those two are repaired. It is medium severity, not critical, because the majority of the metaphors survive.

The cited literal constructions are visible in the text: 'ज़रूरी सतहें मौजूद हैं', the bare 'seams', and 'लक्ष्य है system को reason करना आसान बनाना'. The last is an English verb stranded in a Hindi infinitive and needs reconstruction. Most of the article reads well, so this is a cumulative medium issue. It blocks the 4/5 readability bar only until these are repaired, and I rate it 3, not 4.

The table question 'क्या इसने ... इस्तेमाल करने से बचा?' is a genuine ergative error. The resource title 'Evals से evils से लड़ें!' is awkward. The conclusion-area 'valid JSON consistently produce नहीं कर सकता और ... विफल रहता है' is also flawed. These are real but localized issues, so the grammar dimension needs fixes without being critical. I rate it 3, not 4.

Source requires the combined capability to “produce valid JSON and pick the obvious specialist.” Target instead joins explicit failures: “नहीं कर सकता और … विफल रहता है.” That weakens the production gate by requiring both failures.
